newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Nov 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Nov 23.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Education Minister A.H.S.K. Sadek has said an education policy suiting the need of the time, but not politically biased, will be framed.
Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria has said the government is not considering setting up of any stock exchange in Sylhet, Khulna, Rajshahi or Barisal.

With increase in the number of private universities and allegations of irregularities against many of them, the government has taken steps to assess the status of the universities in the private sector.
At least 65 persons were injured on Friday in gunbattle and clashes between the activists of ruling Awami League and opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) in Sirajganj and Natore districts.
Commerce and Industries Minister Tofael Ahmed has invited Singaporean investors to relocate their investment in Bangladesh as it offers the "best investment opportunity available in the world."
Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria said the government has decided "in principle" to privatise the large state-owned industries by offering their shares.

Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria said in Sylhet on Friday the government was aware of problems of small portfolio investors and that monopoly by a section of people in the capital market would not be allowed further.
Production in the Karnaphuli Paper Mill resumed on Friday after remaining suspended for 18 days, causing a loss of taka 100 million.
